description.value: Frontcountry campground in Kootenay National Park on Highway 93, sitting near the narrow turquoise Marble Canyon limestone gorge and its short suspension-bridge trail. A national park entry pass and camping permit are required; reservations open in January and summer sites fill quickly.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies this as a Parks Canada frontcountry campground in Kootenay National Park along BC-93; the Parks Canada website confirms active operations with 2026 reservation launch dates and online/phone booking. OSM tags directly supply shower=no and power_supply=no, neither contradicted by the website. The website's food-safety section instructs campers to store food in their own vehicles or hard-sided trailers/RVs rather than mentioning any provided bear lockers, so animal-safe food storage cannot be confirmed as an amenity.
concerns: No phone number in OSM record; Kootenay National Park Visitor Centre number (1-250-347-9505, seasonal) is available on the website contact page but is not campground-specific.
OSM drinking_water=unknown; potable water availability could not be confirmed from website content.
OSM maxlength=5 appears unusually short (5 metres) for a campground accepting caravans — likely a data entry error in OSM.
Website contact page notes there is no cellular or Wi-Fi service within Kootenay National Park; emergency telephones are available at marked highway locations — relevant safety context for cyclists.
OSM internet_access=no and mobile_reception=no are consistent with the above.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate, active Parks Canada frontcountry campground on the BC-93 cycling corridor in Kootenay National Park; it is a relevant and useful overnight stop for touring cyclists and belongs in the directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: The campground is part of Kootenay National Park's frontcountry camping network operated by Parks Canada. Food-safety regulations require campers to secure all food and scented items in their own vehicle or hard-sided trailer/RV, suggesting no dedicated bear lockers or food storage boxes are provided.
